text: By 15th level, you have acquired greater mental strength. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

definitions.name: Diamond Soul
definitions.summary: Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws.
text: Beginning at 14th level, your mastery of ki grants you proficiency in all saving throws.

definitions.name: Bonus Proficiency

definitions.name: Breath Weapon
definitions.summary: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy.
text: You can use your action to exhale destructive energy. Your draconic ancestry determines the size, shape, and damage type of the exhalation.

When you use your breath weapon, each creature in the area of the exhalation must make a saving throw, the type of which is determined by your draconic ancestry. The DC for this saving throw equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus. A creature takes 2d6 damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 6th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 16th level.
After you use your breath weapon, you cannot use it again until you complete a short or long rest.

definitions.name: Natural Recovery
definitions.summary: Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature.
text: Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your magical energy by sitting in meditation and communing with nature. During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
For example, when you are a 4th-level druid, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level slot or two 1st-level slots.

actions.name: Natural Recovery
actions.note: During a short rest: pick spent slots with levels adding up to half your druid level (rounded up), none 6th level or higher.

definitions.name: Dark One's Own Luck
definitions.summary: Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor.
text: Starting at 6th level, you can call on your patron to alter fate in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll's effects occur.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

when.text: after seeing the roll, before its effects: spends its use until a short or long rest
after seeing the roll, before its effects: spends its use until a short or long rest

definitions.name: Stroke of Luck
definitions.summary: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to.
text: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

when.text: a failed ability check: the d20 counts as a 20; spends its use until a short or long rest

actions.name: Stroke of Luck: the miss hits
actions.note: An attack that missed a target within range hits instead. Roll its damage from the attack.

definitions.name: Relentless Rage
definitions.summary: Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds.
text: Starting at 11th level, your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're raging and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.

definitions.name: Spell Mastery
definitions.summary: At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will.
text: At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.

definitions.name: Signature Spell
definitions.summary: When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort.
text: When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

definitions.name: Song of Rest
definitions.summary: Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest.
text: Beginning at 2nd level, you can use soothing music or oration to help revitalize your wounded allies during a short rest. If you or any friendly creatures who can hear your performance regain hit points at the end of the short rest by spending one or more Hit Dice, each of those creatures regains an extra 1d6 hit points.
The extra hit points increase when you reach certain levels in this class: to 1d8 at 9th level, to 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

definitions.name: Fiendish Resilience
definitions.summary: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest.
text: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from magical weapons or silver weapons ignores this resistance.

actions.name: Fiendish Resilience
actions.note: When you finish a short or long rest: resistance to the type you pick until you pick another. Magical and silvered weapons ignore it.

definitions.name: Perfect Self
definitions.summary: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.
text: At 20th level, when you roll for initiative and have no ki points remaining, you regain 4 ki points.

definitions.name: Survivor
definitions.summary: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle.
text: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

definitions.name: Fiendish Resilience
definitions.summary: Resistance to the damage type you picked, until you pick another. Magical and silvered weapons ignore it.

definitions.name: Frenzy
definitions.summary: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage.
text: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (as described in appendix A).

actions.name: Frenzy
actions.note: When you rage: frenzy too. Until the rage ends, one melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your later turns; when it ends, one level of exhaustion.

actions.name: Frenzy attack
actions.note: While frenzied: one melee weapon attack. Roll it from your weapons.

definitions.name: Retaliation
definitions.summary: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.
text: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon Attack against that creature.

actions.name: Retaliation

definitions.name: Holy Nimbus
definitions.summary: At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight.
text: At 20th level, as an action, you can emanate an aura of sunlight. For 1 minute, bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
In addition, for the duration, you have advantage on saving throws against spells cast by fiends or undead.

actions.name: Holy Nimbus
actions.note: 1 minute of sunlight around you.

when.text: against a spell cast by a fiend or an undead

definitions.name: Draconic Presence
definitions.summary: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened.
text: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the dread presence of your dragon ancestor, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 sorcery points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration spell), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

actions.name: Draconic Presence
actions.note: A 60-ft aura for 1 minute, with concentration: each hostile creature starting its turn in it makes a Wisdom save or is charmed or frightened until it ends; on a success it's immune for 24 hours.

definitions.name: Dark One's Blessing
definitions.summary: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).
text: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your warlock level (minimum of 1).

actions.name: Dark One's Blessing

definitions.name: Hurl Through Hell
definitions.summary: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes.
text: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly transport the target through the lower planes. The creature disappears and hurtles through a nightmare landscape.

At the end of your next turn, the target returns to the space it previously occupied, or the nearest unoccupied space. If the target is not a fiend, it takes 10d10 psychic damage as it reels from its horrific experience.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

actions.name: Hurl Through Hell

roll.label: psychic damage (not to a fiend), when it returns at the end of your next turn

actions.note: When you hit with an attack: the target vanishes through the lower planes until the end of your next turn.

definitions.name: Potent Cantrip
definitions.summary: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect.
text: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

modifiers.label: Potent Cantrip: a creature that succeeds on its save takes half the damage (no other effect).

definitions.name: Empowered Evocation

text: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

definitions.name: Overchannel
definitions.summary: Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells.
text: Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

definitions.name: Circle of the Land: Arctic
definitions.summary: Your circle spells, always prepared and not counted against the spells you prepare: Hold Person, Spike Growth (3rd); Sleet Storm, Slow (5th); Freedom of Movement, Ice Storm (7th); Commune With Nature, Cone of Cold (9th).
text: The Circle of the Land is made up of mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites through a vast oral tradition. These druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of communities that hold to the Old Faith and serve as advisors to the rulers of those folk. As a member of this circle, your magic is influenced by the land where you were initiated into the circle's mysterious rites.

definitions.summary: Your land's circle spells for 9th level join your always-prepared spells; they come from the land you chose (Circle of the Land).

definitions.name: Bonus Cantrip
definitions.summary: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.
text: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

definitions.name: Primal Champion
definitions.summary: Strength and Constitution each go up by 4, and their maximum becomes 24.
text: At 20th level, you embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

definitions.name: Fiend
definitions.summary: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims.
text: You have made a pact with a fiend from the lower planes of existence, a being whose aims are evil, even if you strive against those aims. Such beings desire the corruption or destruction of all things, ultimately including you. Fiends powerful enough to forge a pact include demon lords such as Demogorgon, Orcus, Fraz'Urb-luu, and Baphomet; archdevils such as Asmodeus, Dispater, Mephistopheles, and Belial; pit fiends and balors that are especially mighty; and ultroloths and other lords of the yugoloths.

definitions.name: Expanded Spell List (Fiend)
definitions.summary: Extra spells added to your warlock list: Burning Hands, Command; Blindness/Deafness, Scorching Ray; Fireball, Stinking Cloud; Fire Shield, Wall of Fire; Flame Strike, Hallow.

definitions.name: Archdruid
definitions.summary: Wild Shape as often as you like; you can ignore the verbal, somatic and costless material parts of your druid spells, in any shape.
text: At 20th level, you can use your Wild Shape an unlimited number of times.

Additionally, you can ignore the verbal and somatic components of your druid spells, as well as any material components that lack a cost and aren't consumed by a spell. You gain this benefit in both your normal shape and your beast shape from Wild Shape.

definitions.name: Sorcerous Restoration
definitions.summary: When you finish a short rest, 4 spent sorcery points come back.
text: At 20th level, you regain 4 expended sorcery points whenever you finish a short rest.

definitions.name: Eldritch Master
definitions.summary: Once per long rest, spend 1 minute entreating your patron: every spent Pact Magic slot comes back.
text: At 20th level, you can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended spell slots from your Pact Magic feature.
Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

actions.name: Eldritch Master
actions.note: 1 minute entreating your patron: all your Pact Magic slots come back.

definitions.name: Foe Slayer
definitions.summary: Once on each of your turns, add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack against one of your favored enemies.
text: At 20th level, you become an unparalleled hunter of your enemies. Once on each of your turns, you can add your Wisdom modifier to the attack roll or the damage roll of an attack you make against one of your favored enemies. You can choose to use this feature before or after the roll, but before any effects of the roll are applied.

when.text: against a favored enemy; once per turn, on this attack or its damage
against a favored enemy; once per turn, if you didn't add it to the attack roll

definitions.name: Divine Intervention Improvement
definitions.summary: Divine Intervention succeeds without a roll.
text: At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.

actions.name: Divine Intervention
actions.note: Your deity intervenes, no roll needed; the DM chooses how. Then not again for 7 days.

definitions.name: Persistent Rage
definitions.summary: Your rage ends early only if you fall unconscious or choose to end it (it still lasts at most 1 minute).
text: Beginning at 15th level, your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

definitions.name: Indomitable Might
definitions.summary: A Strength check whose total is below your Strength score uses the score instead.
text: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

definitions.name: Mindless Rage
definitions.summary: While raging you can't be charmed or frightened; one that's on you is suspended for the rage.
text: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

definitions.name: Purity of Body
definitions.summary: Immune to disease and poison: poison damage and the poisoned condition.
text: At 10th level, your mastery of the ki flowing through you makes you immune to disease and poison.

definitions.name: Divine Health
definitions.summary: Immune to disease.
text: By 3rd level, the divine magic flowing through you makes you immune to disease.

definitions.name: Nature's Ward
definitions.summary: Immune to poison and disease; elementals and fey can't charm or frighten you.
text: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

modifiers.label: Nature's Ward: an elemental or a fey can't charm or frighten you.

definitions.name: Empty Body
definitions.summary: 4 ki, an action: invisible for 1 minute, with resistance to every damage type except force. 8 ki: cast Astral Projection without material components (yourself only).
text: Beginning at 18th level, you can use your action to spend 4 ki points to become invisible for 1 minute. During that time, you also have resistance to all damage but force damage.
Additionally, you can spend 8 ki points to cast the astral projection spell, without needing material components. When you do so, you can't take any other creatures with you.

spells.name: Astral Projection
spells.casting: 8 ki, no material components, yourself only

actions.name: Empty Body
actions.note: Invisible for 1 minute, and resistance to all damage except force.

definitions.name: Stillness of Mind
definitions.summary: An action: end one effect on you that charms or frightens you.
text: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

actions.name: Stillness of Mind
actions.note: Ends one effect on you that charms or frightens you.

definitions.name: Cleansing Touch
definitions.summary: An action, uses equal to your Charisma modifier (at least 1) per long rest: end one spell on you or on a willing creature you touch.
text: Beginning at 14th level, you can use your action to end one spell on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (a minimum of once). You regain expended uses when you finish a long rest.

actions.name: Cleansing Touch
actions.note: End one spell on you or on a willing creature you touch. On you: remove its tag.

definitions.name: Purity of Spirit
definitions.summary: Always under Protection from Evil and Good (shown as a tag).
text: Beginning at 15th level, you are always under the effects of a protection from evil and good spell.

definitions.name: Thief's Reflexes
definitions.summary: In the first round of a combat you take two turns: one at your initiative, one at your initiative minus 10 (not when surprised).
text: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can't use this feature when you are surprised.

modifiers.label: Thief's Reflexes: a second turn in the first round, at this total minus 10 (not when surprised).

definitions.name: Divine Intervention
definitions.summary: Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.
text: Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your deity to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

Imploring your deity's aid requires you to use your action. Describe the assistance you seek, and roll percentile dice. If you roll a number equal to or lower than your cleric level, your deity intervenes. The GM chooses the nature of the intervention; the effect of any cleric spell or cleric domain spell would be appropriate.
If your deity intervenes, you can't use this feature again for 7 days. Otherwise, you can use it again after you finish a long rest.
At 20th level, your call for intervention succeeds automatically, no roll required.

actions.name: Divine Intervention

roll.label: your cleric level or lower: your deity intervenes

actions.note: Call on your deity: roll d100, and if it's your cleric level or lower, the DM chooses how it helps. On a success, not again for 7 days; otherwise after a long rest.
